big_picture_notes: Jeremiah is a non‑linear anthology of oracles, laments, sign‑acts, and narratives compiled across the prophet’s long ministry. The macro‑structure is modular: large narrative superscriptions mark major collections, while oracle formulas ('The word of the LORD came…', 'Thus says the LORD') are the key scene markers—each scene a single, complete divine speech or report ideal for memorization. The MT places the Oracles Against the Nations at 46–51 (LXX relocates after 25:13), underscoring the book’s editorial history. Thematic glue: relentless covenant lawsuit against Judah, the 'enemy from the north' motif, the prophet’s confessions, and a hope‑center in the Book of Consolation (30–33). Memorize by literary units (oracles), not chronology.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Jeremiah 1 is a distinct proem: formal superscription, first call‑oracle, two commissioning visions (almond branch, boiling pot), and the fortified‑prophet metaphors. Start (1:1): superscription. End (1:19): promise 'I am with you… to deliver you'—inclusio with 1:8. Literary Glue: call dialogue and paired visions leading to charge/promise.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The words of Jeremiah the priest, set across the reigns from Josiah to the exile.

scenes.scene_name: Before I Formed You in the Womb
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call: God's prenatal appointment as a prophet to the nations, and Jeremiah's 'I am only a child.'

scenes.scene_name: I Have Put My Words in Your Mouth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The reassurance and the touched mouth — set over nations 'to uproot… to build and plant.'
The first vision and its wordplay: God watching (shoqed) over His word like the almond (shaqed).

scenes.scene_name: The Boiling Pot from the North
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The second vision interpreting the coming disaster summoned from the north.

scenes.scene_name: A Fortified City, an Iron Pillar
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The final charge: stand and speak, made an unbreakable wall — 'I am with you to deliver you.'

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Jeremiah 2–25 is the core pre‑exilic oracle collection: covenant lawsuit, unfaithful wife/vine/cistern metaphors, 'enemy from the north,' temple sermon, confessions, sign‑acts, and the cup of wrath climax. Start (2:1): 'The word of the LORD came…' End (25:38): desolation after the universal cup. Literary Glue: repeated oracle markers and motifs; 25:1–14 functions as hinge/summary of 23 years.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The lawsuit opens tenderly: Israel as a bride who followed God in the wilderness, holy as His firstfruits.

scenes.scene_name: What Fault Did Your Fathers Find?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The charge of forgetting the Exodus-God, the priests and prophets who no longer sought Him.
The heart of the indictment — forsaking the fountain of living water for broken cisterns.

scenes.scene_name: Your Own Evil Will Discipline You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel become prey for forsaking the LORD, gaining nothing from Egypt or Assyria.
The harlotry on every high hill, the stain of guilt no soap can wash.

scenes.scene_name: A Wild Donkey in Her Heat
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The denial of defilement met by the image of uncontrollable craving for foreign gods.

scenes.scene_name: Where Are the Gods You Made?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel disgraced like a caught thief, calling a tree 'father' yet crying 'save us' in trouble.
The rebellious generation that treats God as a wilderness, forgetting Him days without number.

scenes.scene_name: You Will Be Disappointed by Egypt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The blood-stained skirts and the false plea 'I am innocent,' ending in shame over trusted allies.
The divorce-law applied: a defiled land and a people who lay in wait for lovers like a desert nomad.

scenes.scene_name: The Brazen Look of a Prostitute
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Withheld rains and false endearments — 'My Father' — while still doing all the evil they can.

scenes.scene_name: Faithless Israel and Her Sister Judah
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The certificate of divorce given to Israel, which faithless Judah saw yet did not fear.
Judah's return in pretense, making her guiltier than her adulterous sister.
The merciful call northward: only acknowledge your guilt and I will not be angry forever.
The gathering of one from a city and two from a family, given true shepherds.
The day the ark is forgotten and all nations gather to Jerusalem, Judah and Israel reunited.
God's longing to call them sons, against their betrayal like an unfaithful wife.

scenes.scene_name: Return, and I Will Heal Your Faithlessness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The weeping on the heights and the people's answering confession — 'salvation is in the LORD.'

scenes.scene_name: Let Us Lie Down in Our Shame
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The confession that the shameful god has devoured their inheritance from their youth.

scenes.scene_name: If You Will Return, O Israel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The promise that the nations will be blessed if Israel truly returns and swears in truth.
Break up the unplowed ground and remove the foreskins of the heart, lest wrath break out like fire.
Blow the ram's horn and flee to the fortified cities before the coming destruction.
The destroyer of nations advancing; sackcloth and a failing of nerve in king and priest.
Jeremiah's protest at the deception of 'peace,' and the wind too strong to winnow.

scenes.scene_name: Wash the Evil from Your Heart
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The enemy advancing like clouds, the urgent plea for Jerusalem to be cleansed.
A besieging army surrounding the rebel city — 'how bitter… it pierces the heart!'

scenes.scene_name: My Anguish! I Writhe in Pain
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The prophet's agony at the alarm of battle and the land laid waste.
God's verdict that His people are foolish, and the un-creation vision of a dark, empty earth.
The quaking mountains, the vanished birds and men, the cities torn down before His anger.

scenes.scene_name: Desolate, but Not a Full End
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The mourning earth and darkened heavens, every city fleeing the horseman.

scenes.scene_name: The Cry of the Daughter of Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The doomed city adorning herself in vain, gasping like a woman in labor before murderers.
If a single honest person can be found, God will forgive — yet they swear falsely.
Neither poor nor powerful know the way of the LORD; all have broken the yoke.
A lion and wolf to strike them down for forsaking God and committing adultery.
Ravaging the vineyards of the unfaithful, who lie 'harm will not come to us.'
God's word made fire, an ancient nation brought to devour harvest, sons, and flocks.
Not a full end, but the just sentence: as you served foreign gods, so you will serve foreigners.

scenes.scene_name: The Sand as the Boundary for the Sea
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The senseless people who will not fear the One who bounds the surging sea.
The stubborn hearts that never say 'let us fear the LORD' who gives the rains.

scenes.scene_name: They Do Not Defend the Needy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Wicked men like fowlers, grown fat and sleek, ignoring the fatherless — 'should I not punish?'
The horrible thing in the land: false prophets and self-ruling priests loved by the people.
The alarm to Benjamin as disaster looms from the north against the Daughter of Zion.
The attackers' war-cry to strike at noon and by night against her fortresses.
The city to be punished for the oppression that gushes from her like water.

scenes.scene_name: I Am Full of the LORD's Wrath
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The remnant gleaned, the closed ears, the prophet weary of holding back God's fury.

scenes.scene_name: Peace, Peace, When There Is No Peace
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The greedy from prophet to priest who heal the wound lightly and cannot blush.
'Where is the good way?' — but they refused to walk in it or heed the watchmen.

scenes.scene_name: Your Burnt Offerings Are Not Acceptable
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Disaster as the fruit of their schemes; frankincense from Sheba unwanted.
Stumbling blocks set, a cruel and merciless nation roaring like the sea against Zion.
Limp hands and labor-pangs; the call to mourn in sackcloth for an only son.
Jeremiah the assayer testing a people of bronze and iron — refining that cannot purge them.
Stand in the gate: do not trust the deceptive chant 'the temple of the LORD.'
The condition for dwelling in the land: justice, and no oppression of the foreigner, orphan, and widow.
Stealing and murdering, then standing in God's house — has it become a den of robbers?
What God did to Shiloh He will do to the trusted temple, casting them from His presence.

scenes.scene_name: Cakes for the Queen of Heaven
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The command not to pray for them, who provoke God with family-wide idolatry.

scenes.scene_name: My Anger Will Be Poured Out
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Their self-spiting provocation answered by unquenchable fury on land and beast.

scenes.scene_name: Obey Me, and I Will Be Your God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Not sacrifices but obedience was the original command at the Exodus.
Generations of sent prophets ignored, each more evil than the last.
The nation that will not listen; raise a lamentation on the barren heights.
Abominations in God's house and child-sacrifice He never commanded.
Topheth renamed for the coming dead, joy and the bridegroom's voice removed.
The desecration of the dead who worshiped the host of heaven, choosing death over life.
No one repents asking 'what have I done?' — each charging on like a horse into battle.

scenes.scene_name: The Lying Pen of the Scribes
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Even the stork knows her seasons, but the wise who reject God's word are put to shame.
The greedy from least to greatest, healing the wound lightly with 'peace, peace.'

scenes.scene_name: We Hoped for Peace, but Terror
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The harvest taken away, the doomed people fleeing to the fortified cities.
The snorting horses from Dan and the serpents God will send among them.

scenes.scene_name: Is the LORD No Longer in Zion?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The prophet's faint heart and the people's cry — 'the harvest has passed… we are not saved.'

scenes.scene_name: Is There No Balm in Gilead?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The crushed prophet mourning the unhealed brokenness of his people.

scenes.scene_name: Oh, That My Head Were a Spring of Water
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The prophet's longing to weep day and night and to flee his faithless, adulterous people.

scenes.scene_name: They Bend Their Tongues Like Bows
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A society of liars and slanderers where no one tells the truth, refusing to know God.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Refine and Test Them
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Deadly-arrow tongues speaking peace while setting traps — 'should I not punish them?'

scenes.scene_name: A Heap of Rubble, a Haunt for Jackals
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Weeping for the scorched mountains as Jerusalem and Judah are made desolate.
The wise question answered: because they forsook God's law and would not obey His voice.
Judgment for following the Baals: scattered among unknown nations, pursued by the sword.
The call for professional mourners as the sound of wailing rises from Zion.

scenes.scene_name: Death Has Climbed Through Our Windows
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Teach the daughters to lament, for corpses will fall like dung in the open field.

scenes.scene_name: Let Him Boast That He Knows Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Not wisdom, strength, or riches, but knowing the LORD who delights in steadfast love and justice.
The coming punishment of all who are circumcised only in the flesh, Judah among the nations.

scenes.scene_name: Idols Are Scarecrows That Cannot Speak
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Do not learn the ways of the nations whose hand-made idols can do neither harm nor good.

scenes.scene_name: There Is None Like You, O King of Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The incomparable greatness of the LORD whom all should fear.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Is the True God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The senseless idol-worshipers contrasted with the living God and eternal King.

scenes.scene_name: He Made the Earth by His Power
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The perishing false gods against the Creator who stretched out the heavens by His understanding.
Every goldsmith shamed by his breathless idols, but Jacob's Portion is the Maker of all.
The command to those under siege as God flings out the inhabitants of the land.
The prophet's lament for his ruined tent and the senseless shepherds who scattered the flock.

scenes.scene_name: A Man's Way Is Not His Own
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The commotion from the north, and the confession that no one directs his own steps.
The plea for measured discipline and for wrath on the nations that devoured Jacob.

scenes.scene_name: Cursed Is the Man Who Disobeys
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The words of the covenant proclaimed — 'Obey Me… and I will be your God' — answered 'Amen, LORD.'
Repeated warnings since the Exodus ignored, so God brought the covenant curses.
Judah returned to the sins of the fathers, breaking the covenant.

scenes.scene_name: Gods as Numerous as Your Cities
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: An inescapable disaster coming, the many altars of Baal unable to save.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Pray for These People
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The command against intercession, for no consecrated meat can avert their doom.

scenes.scene_name: A Flourishing Olive Tree Set on Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The once-beautiful tree decreed for burning because of the incense to Baal.

scenes.scene_name: A Gentle Lamb Led to Slaughter
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jeremiah's first lament: the plot against his life and his plea to see God's vengeance.
Judgment on the prophet's own townsmen who sought his life — no remnant left.

scenes.scene_name: Why Does the Way of the Wicked Prosper?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The prophet's complaint about the faithless who have God on their lips but far from their hearts.

scenes.scene_name: Drag Them Away Like Sheep to Slaughter
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The plea to set the wicked apart for judgment as the mourning land withers.

scenes.scene_name: If You Have Raced with Men on Foot
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's bracing answer — and the warning that even his own family has betrayed him.
God giving the beloved of His soul, become a roaring lion, into enemy hands.

scenes.scene_name: Many Shepherds Have Destroyed My Vineyard
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The trampled, desolate inheritance that no one takes to heart.

scenes.scene_name: The Sword of the LORD Devours
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Destroyers on every height; they sowed wheat but harvested thorns.
The evil neighbors uprooted, yet promised return to their own inheritance.
The nations established among God's people if they learn His ways, or uprooted if they refuse.
The first command of the sign-act: a loincloth worn but kept from water.
The loincloth concealed in a crevice of the rocks by the river.

scenes.scene_name: It Was Ruined, of No Use
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The retrieved loincloth found rotted and worthless.

scenes.scene_name: So I Will Ruin the Pride of Judah
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The meaning: as the loincloth clings to the waist, so Israel was made to cling to God — but would not listen.
The riddle of drunkenness: God filling king, priest, and people to smash them against one another.
The plea against pride, with the prophet weeping in secret over the captive flock.
The word to king and queen mother as all Judah is carried into exile.

scenes.scene_name: Why Has This Happened to Me?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The flock entrusted and lost, the exposed shame answered by 'the magnitude of your iniquity.'

scenes.scene_name: Can the Ethiopian Change His Skin?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The impossibility of doing good for those accustomed to evil — scattered like chaff.

scenes.scene_name: How Long Will You Remain Unclean?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The exposed shame of Jerusalem's adulteries seen by God.
Judah mourning, the empty cisterns, the cracked ground, the ashamed farmers.

scenes.scene_name: Even the Doe Deserts Her Fawn
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wild creatures fainting for lack of grass and pasture.

scenes.scene_name: O Hope of Israel, Why Like a Stranger?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The people's plea owning their iniquity yet asking God not to forsake them.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Pray for This People
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God refusing their fasts and offerings, to finish them by sword, famine, and plague.
Jeremiah's protest about the false 'peace,' answered by God's disavowal of the prophets.

scenes.scene_name: These Prophets Will Meet Their End
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sword and famine on the lying prophets and the people who heeded them.
The crushing wound of the virgin daughter, prophet and priest wandering a strange land.
The communal confession and plea to the only God who can send rain — 'we put our hope in You.'
No intercession could turn God's heart; the destinies of death, sword, famine, and captivity.

scenes.scene_name: I Am Weary of Showing Compassion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A horror among the kingdoms because of Manasseh — 'who will have pity on you, O Jerusalem?'

scenes.scene_name: The Mother of Seven Grows Faint
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Winnowed at the gates, widows multiplied, the bereaved mother's sun setting at noon.
The prophet's lament of being cursed by all, and God's promise to deliver him for good.
Iron from the north unbreakable; enslavement decreed for Judah's sins.
'I ate Your words' — the prophet bearing God's name and enduring reproach for His honor.
The lonely, indignant prophet with an incurable wound, accusing God of being a mirage.
God's answer: if Jeremiah returns and speaks what is noble, he will be made an unbreakable wall.
The sign-act of celibacy in a land where children will die unburied.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Enter a House of Mourning
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's peace, love, and compassion removed, the dead unmourned and unburied.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Enter a House of Feasting
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sounds of joy and the bridegroom's voice to be removed before their eyes.

scenes.scene_name: Why Has He Pronounced This Disaster?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The answer: because the fathers forsook God, and they did worse — cast out to serve other gods.

scenes.scene_name: Brought Up from the Land of the North
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A future oath that will eclipse the Exodus, as God returns the exiles to their land.
The hunters sent for the guilty whose ways are not hidden — repaid double for defiling the land.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Know My Name Is the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The nations coming from the ends of the earth, confessing their fathers' idols were lies.

scenes.scene_name: The Sin of Judah Engraved with Iron
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Judah's sin written on the tablets of their hearts and the horns of their altars.
The forfeited inheritance and enslavement, for they kindled God's everlasting anger.

scenes.scene_name: Cursed Is the Man Who Trusts in Flesh
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The one trusting mankind like a desert shrub that never sees prosperity come.

scenes.scene_name: Blessed Is the Man Who Trusts in the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Like a tree planted by the waters, unafraid of heat or drought, ever bearing fruit.

scenes.scene_name: The Heart Is Deceitful Above All Things
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The unsearchable heart that the LORD examines, and the partridge of ill-gotten gain.

scenes.scene_name: The Fountain of Living Water Forsaken
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The glorious throne of the sanctuary, and the shame of all who abandon the LORD.

scenes.scene_name: Heal Me, and I Will Be Healed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The prophet's plea against the taunt 'where is the word of the LORD?', not shrinking from his call.

scenes.scene_name: You Are My Refuge in the Day of Disaster
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The plea that his persecutors, not he, be put to shame and shattered.

scenes.scene_name: Stand at the Gate of the People
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Sabbath sermon: hear the word, O kings and people of Judah at the gates.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Carry a Load on the Sabbath
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The command to keep the Sabbath holy, which the fathers refused with stiffened necks.

scenes.scene_name: Then Kings Will Enter These Gates
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The promise of an enduring, inhabited city if they keep the Sabbath.

scenes.scene_name: An Unquenchable Fire in the Gates
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Offerings brought from all Judah if they obey — but unquenchable fire if they do not.
The sign at the potter's house: the flawed vessel reshaped as the potter saw fit.

scenes.scene_name: Like Clay in the Potter's Hand
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's word: 'can I not treat you as this potter?' — Israel as clay in His hand.

scenes.scene_name: If a Nation Turns, I Will Relent
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The principle of conditional judgment and blessing on nations that turn or do evil.

scenes.scene_name: It Is Hopeless; We Will Follow Our Own Plans
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to turn met by the people's defiant refusal.
The unheard-of horror: Israel forsaking the ancient roads for rutted bypaths.
Their land made a perpetual scorn, God showing them His back in calamity.
The conspiracy to denounce him, and his plea — 'should good be repaid with evil?'

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Blot Out Their Sin
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The prophet's imprecation against those who dug a pit for his life.
The sign-act command: a potter's jar taken to the Valley of Ben-hinnom.

scenes.scene_name: Disaster to Make the Ears Ring
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Judgment for filling the place with innocent blood and burning children to Baal.
Topheth renamed; their plans ruined and their corpses given to the birds.

scenes.scene_name: They Will Eat Their Own Children
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The city made a horror, reduced to cannibalism in the siege.
The smashed jar as a sign: 'I will shatter this nation… never again to be repaired.'
Jerusalem's rooftops where they burned incense to the host of heaven.
Jeremiah in the temple court declaring the coming judgment on the stiff-necked city.
Pashhur beating Jeremiah and putting him in the stocks, renamed for the coming terror.
The doom on Pashhur and the city — exile and death in Babylon.

scenes.scene_name: A Fire Shut Up in My Bones
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The bitter lament: deceived and mocked, yet unable to keep silent God's burning word.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Is with Me Like a Warrior
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The whispering of friends against him, met by confidence that his persecutors will fail.
The plea to see God's vengeance, breaking into praise for rescuing the needy.

scenes.scene_name: Cursed Be the Day I Was Born
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The dark turn of the lament cursing his own birth.

scenes.scene_name: Why Did I Come Out of the Womb?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The depth of despair, wishing he had died unborn — the bleakest of the confessions.
The king's hope for a miracle as Nebuchadnezzar besieges the city.

scenes.scene_name: I Myself Will Fight Against You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God turning their own weapons back and striking the city with plague.

scenes.scene_name: The Way of Life and the Way of Death
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Zedekiah handed over; whoever surrenders to the Chaldeans will live as a spoil of war.
The charge to the house of David lest God's wrath go forth like unquenchable fire.
Judgment on the complacent city — 'I will kindle a fire in your forest.'

scenes.scene_name: Go Down to the King's Palace
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to administer justice and not wrong the foreigner, orphan, and widow.
The conditional oath: obedience brings enthroned kings, disobedience ruin.

scenes.scene_name: Like Gilead, Turned to a Desert
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The palace of cedar to be cut down and burned by appointed destroyers.

scenes.scene_name: Why Has the LORD Done This?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The nations' question answered: because they forsook the covenant for other gods.

scenes.scene_name: Weep for the Exile Who Will Never Return
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The word on Shallum (Jehoahaz), who will die in the land of his exile.

scenes.scene_name: Woe to Him Who Builds by Unrighteousness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The condemnation of the king who builds a cedar palace on unpaid labor.

scenes.scene_name: Is This Not What It Means to Know Me?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Josiah's justice to the poor contrasted with the son's eyes set on dishonest gain.
Jehoiakim to be dragged out and thrown beyond the gates, unmourned.
The cry to Lebanon as the lovers are crushed, a way of rebellion from youth.

scenes.scene_name: Pangs Like a Woman in Labor
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The shepherds driven off by the wind, the cedar-nestled city groaning in anguish.

scenes.scene_name: Coniah the Signet Ring Pulled Off
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jehoiachin handed to Nebuchadnezzar and hurled into a foreign land to die.
The longing-but-never-returning king cast out like an unwanted jar.
The land summoned to hear: none of Coniah's line will sit on David's throne.

scenes.scene_name: Woe to the Shepherds Who Scatter
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Judgment on the leaders who destroyed and scattered the sheep of God's pasture.
The promise to regather the flock and raise up faithful shepherds.
The coming Davidic King — 'The LORD Our Righteousness' — who reigns in justice.

scenes.scene_name: Brought Up from the Land of the North
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A future oath surpassing the Exodus as God restores Israel to her land.

scenes.scene_name: My Heart Is Broken Within Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The prophet shaken over the adulterous, cursed land and its evil prophets.
Wickedness even in God's house, their path made slick into darkness.
The Baal-prophets of Samaria and the adulterous prophets of Jerusalem fed wormwood.
The visions of their own minds, promising peace to those who despise God.
None stood in the LORD's council; His anger will not turn until His purpose is done.

scenes.scene_name: I Did Not Send These Prophets
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Had they stood in His council, they would have turned the people from evil.

scenes.scene_name: Do I Not Fill Heaven and Earth?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The God near and far from whom no one can hide in secret.

scenes.scene_name: I Had a Dream! I Had a Dream!
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The lying dreamers who would make the people forget God's name as the fathers forgot it for Baal.

scenes.scene_name: Is Not My Word Like Fire?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Straw against grain — God's word a fire and a hammer that smashes rock.
God's threefold opposition to those who steal, wag their tongues, and tell false dreams.

scenes.scene_name: What Is the Burden of the LORD?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wordplay on 'burden' — 'What burden? I will forsake you.'

scenes.scene_name: Refer No More to the Burden
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The corrected speech: ask only 'what has the LORD spoken?'
Judgment on those who keep claiming 'the burden of the LORD' against His command.
The vision after Jeconiah's exile: very good figs and figs too bad to eat.
The exiles regarded as good, to be returned and given a heart to know the LORD.
Those left in the land and in Egypt given to sword, famine, and plague.
The summary oracle: the word spoken again and again, but they would not listen.
The prophets' unheeded call not to provoke God with idols.
The families of the north summoned against the land for its disobedience.
Joy removed and the whole land made a desolation under Babylon for seventy years.
After the seventy years, the Chaldeans judged for their guilt per all that is written.

scenes.scene_name: The Cup of the Wine of Wrath
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cup taken from God's hand for all the nations to drink and stagger.

scenes.scene_name: I Made All the Nations Drink
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jerusalem and Judah first, then Pharaoh and Egypt.
The roll of nations given the cup of wrath.
The far nations and, last of all, the king of Babylon himself.
The command to drink, for judgment begins at the city that bears God's Name.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD Will Roar from on High
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The LORD bringing a charge against all the nations, treading them like grapes.

scenes.scene_name: Disaster Spreading from Nation to Nation
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A rising storm; the slain of the LORD spread like dung across the earth.
The leaders shattered like fine pottery, with no escape from the slaughter.

scenes.scene_name: He Has Left His Den Like a Lion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The peaceful meadows silenced under the LORD's fierce anger — the climax of Story B.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Jeremiah 26–29 shifts to prose biography: court trial, symbolic yokes, conflict with Hananiah, letters with exiles and Shemaiah. Start (26:1): historical superscription. End (29:32): verdict against Shemaiah. Literary Glue: prose style, dated formulas, true vs false prophecy theme.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The temple-sermon narrative: speak every word, perhaps they will turn and God will relent.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Make This House Like Shiloh
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The conditional threat that the temple and city will become a curse if they will not listen.
The priests and prophets seizing Jeremiah for prophesying against the temple.

scenes.scene_name: This Man Is Worthy of Death
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The officials convening as the charge is laid before them.
Jeremiah's defense — 'the LORD sent me' — warning them not to shed innocent blood.
The verdict of acquittal, citing Micah and Hezekiah who feared the LORD and were spared.
The grim counter-example: Uriah, who prophesied the same and fled to Egypt.
Uriah brought back and killed, but Ahikam shielding Jeremiah from death.
The sign-act: a yoke worn and a message sent to the surrounding kings.

scenes.scene_name: I Have Given It to Nebuchadnezzar
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Creator placing all lands under His servant the king of Babylon.

scenes.scene_name: Put Your Neck Under the Yoke
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Punishment for nations that refuse; the nation that serves Babylon will remain in its land.
The same word to Zedekiah: why die by sword, famine, and plague?

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Listen to the Prophets
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The false prophets who say 'do not serve Babylon' will perish with those who heed them.

scenes.scene_name: The Articles Will Not Be Brought Back
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The lie that the temple vessels will soon return; let the true prophets plead instead.

scenes.scene_name: Carried to Babylon Until I Attend to Them
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The remaining vessels to go to Babylon until the day God restores them.
The rival prophet's claim that within two years God will break Babylon's yoke.

scenes.scene_name: Recognized Only If It Comes True
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jeremiah's 'Amen' and the test: a prophet of peace is proven only by fulfillment.
Hananiah breaking the yoke off Jeremiah's neck before the people.

scenes.scene_name: A Yoke of Iron in Its Place
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's answer: the broken wooden yoke replaced by an unbreakable iron one.
The sentence on the false prophet who taught rebellion — and its swift fulfillment.
Jeremiah's letter sent from Jerusalem to the captives in Babylon.

scenes.scene_name: Seek the Prosperity of the City
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Build houses, plant gardens, and pray for Babylon — 'if it prospers, you too will prosper.'

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Be Deceived by Your Prophets
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The warning against the diviners falsely prophesying in God's name.

scenes.scene_name: Plans to Give You a Future and a Hope
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: After seventy years God's promise to restore — 'I know the plans I have for you.'

scenes.scene_name: You Will Seek Me and Find Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The promise of restoration to those who call and search with all their heart.
Judgment of sword, famine, and plague on the king and people left in the city.
The pursued remnant made a horror, for ignoring the prophets sent again and again.

scenes.scene_name: Ahab and Zedekiah, the Lying Prophets
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The two false prophets in Babylon to be handed to Nebuchadnezzar.
The curse drawn from their fate for their adultery and lies in God's name.
Shemaiah's counter-letter demanding Zephaniah rebuke Jeremiah.
Shemaiah's complaint that Jeremiah told the exiles to settle in for a long stay.
The verdict on Shemaiah for preaching rebellion — no descendant to see the coming good.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Jeremiah 30–33 is a 'book within the book'—explicitly commanded to be written—uniting restoration themes: healing, rebuilding, new covenant, and sign‑act purchase. Start (30:1–2): write in a book. End (33:26): restoration promise. Literary Glue: 'restore the fortunes,' 'my people Israel/Judah,' physical to spiritual renewal arc.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Book of Consolation opens: a command to record God's promise to restore Israel and Judah.
A cry of terror, men in labor-like anguish — yet 'he will be saved out of it.'

scenes.scene_name: They Will Serve David Their King
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The broken yoke and the promise of the raised-up Davidic king.

scenes.scene_name: Do Not Be Afraid, O Jacob
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Salvation from a distant land, with just discipline but not complete destruction.
The grievous injury for which there seems no remedy or healer.
The forgotten lovers and the wound inflicted because of great iniquity.
The devourers devoured and Zion the outcast healed.

scenes.scene_name: The City Rebuilt on Her Ruins
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Restored fortunes, thanksgiving and celebration, oppressors punished.
A ruler arising from their own midst, brought near to God — the covenant formula.
The whirlwind of fury that will not turn back until His purpose is accomplished.
God the God of all Israel's families, who gave rest to the sword's survivors.

scenes.scene_name: I Have Loved You with an Everlasting Love
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Virgin Israel rebuilt, taking up tambourines again in joyful dancing.

scenes.scene_name: Let Us Go Up to Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Vineyards replanted on Samaria and watchmen calling the pilgrims to the LORD.
Gathering the blind, lame, and laboring from the north, led weeping beside streams of water.
The Scatterer become Shepherd, ransoming Jacob to radiant joy on Zion's heights.
Maidens and elders rejoicing, the priests filled with God's abundance.
The voice in Ramah comforted by the promise that the children will return.

scenes.scene_name: Restore Me, That I May Return
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Ephraim's repentant moaning after severe discipline.

scenes.scene_name: Is Not Ephraim a Precious Son?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's yearning heart, the call to return, and the 'new thing' created in the land.
Judah's restored blessing and God's refreshing of the weary soul.
The pleasant waking, and God watching to build and plant as once to uproot.

scenes.scene_name: Each Will Die for His Own Iniquity
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The end of the sour-grapes proverb: individual responsibility.
The promise of a covenant unlike the broken one made at the Exodus.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Write It on Their Hearts
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The heart of the New Covenant: God's law within, all knowing Him, sins remembered no more.

scenes.scene_name: As Sure as the Fixed Order
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Israel's enduring nationhood guaranteed by the unbreakable order of sun, moon, and sea.

scenes.scene_name: The City Holy to the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The rebuilt Jerusalem, even the valley of corpses made holy, never again uprooted.
The setting: the besieged city and the prophet confined in the courtyard of the guard.
Zedekiah's charge against Jeremiah's word that the city will fall to Babylon.
Hanamel's coming to sell, confirming the word of the LORD to redeem the field.

scenes.scene_name: I Signed and Sealed the Deed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The purchase weighed out and the deed entrusted to Baruch before witnesses.
The deeds preserved in a clay jar as a sign of future restoration.

scenes.scene_name: Nothing Is Too Difficult for You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jeremiah's prayer to the Creator, great in counsel and mighty in deed.

scenes.scene_name: You Brought Israel Out of Egypt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The recital of God's signs and the gift of the land they failed to obey.

scenes.scene_name: Yet You Said, Buy the Field
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The perplexity: siege ramps mounted, yet the command to purchase land.

scenes.scene_name: Is Anything Too Difficult for Me?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's answer affirming the city's delivery into Chaldean hands.

scenes.scene_name: They Have Done Nothing but Evil
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The city burned for the Baal-worship that provoked God from its founding.
The abominations in God's house and the child-sacrifice He never commanded.
The turn to hope: regathered to dwell in safety as His people.
One heart and one way, God rejoicing to do them good and plant them faithfully.
The sign fulfilled: deeds signed in a restored land, captivity reversed.

scenes.scene_name: Call to Me, and I Will Answer
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The second word in confinement: great and unsearchable things to be revealed.
The torn-down houses to be filled with the slain of God's wrath.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Bring Health and Healing
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The promise to heal and restore Judah and Israel as in former times.
Forgiveness of all their sin, the city made a renown and joy among the nations.

scenes.scene_name: The Voice of the Bride and Bridegroom
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Joy and thanksgiving returning to the desolate places — 'the LORD is good.'
Flocks passing under the counter's hand in the restored cities of Judah.
The fulfilled promise: a righteous Branch for David, 'The LORD Our Righteousness.'

scenes.scene_name: David Will Never Lack a Man
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The enduring Davidic throne and Levitical priesthood.

scenes.scene_name: As Sure as Day and Night
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The covenant with David as unbreakable as the covenant with day and night.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Have Compassion on Them
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Against the taunt that God rejected His two families — His sworn restoration.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Jeremiah 34–45 resumes prose, tracing final siege, fall, and aftermath in Judah and Egypt, concluding with Baruch’s oracle. Start (34:1): precise siege setting. End (45:5): life as prize of war promise to Baruch. Literary Glue: chronological thread through collapse and remnant’s disobedience.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Word during siege; personal fate of Zedekiah—complete oracle unit.
Manumission made and revoked; covenant broken; judgment announced—narrative oracle.
Obedient clan contrasts Judah’s disobedience; perpetual promise to Rechab’s line.
Baruch writes/reads; king burns; new scroll dictated—complete scroll cycle narrative.
Prophet cast into the pit; Ebed‑melech’s rescue—compact deliverance scene.
Capture and aftermath; Ebed‑melech promised life—wraps siege narrative.
Governor installed → assassination → remnant’s inquiry and disobedience—multi‑part narrative unit.
Sign‑act bricks at Tahpanhes; indictment of queen of heaven worship—judgment on remnant in Egypt.
Personal word—seek not great things; life given as booty—narrative colophon.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Jeremiah 46–51 comprises the international judgment block (Egypt, Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar/Hazor, Elam, and culminates with Babylon). Start (46:1): collection superscription. End (51:64): 'Thus far the words of Jeremiah'—editorial colophon. Literary Glue: nation‑by‑nation judgment sequence with oracle formulas and refrain motifs.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Defeat at the Euphrates; flee, O mighty ones—complete battle oracle.
Nebuchadnezzar strikes Egypt; Israel reassured—paired oracle unit.
Waters rising from the north; sword of the LORD—short nation oracle.
Extensive dirge and taunt with restoration note—long composite oracle.
Rhetorical questions about Milcom; restoration in latter days—compact unit.
Wisdom failed in Teman; eagle soars—complete oracle.
Hamath and Arpad dismayed; palace consumed by fire—short unit.
Plundered nomads; dwell in the deep—brief oracle.
Bow of Elam broken; latter‑day restoration—compact verdict.
Massive anti‑Babylon corpus culminating with scroll sinking at Euphrates—collection capstone with colophon.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Jeremiah 52 is a third‑person historical chronicle paralleling 2 Kings 24:18–25:30, separated by the colophon (51:64). Purpose: confirm fulfillment historically. Start (52:1): regnal formula. End (52:34): Jehoiachin’s daily allowance. Literary Glue: continuous prose narrative of fall, exile, and minor grace note.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Standard regnal rubric ending in rebellion—introductory summary.
Siege account through deportation and remnant—single fall narrative.
Inventory of bronze pillars and vessels—loss catalog scene.
Captives taken and tallied—human cost registry.
Elevation in Babylon—final glimmer closing the book.
